https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: Minutes of the regular Troy Board of Education meeting held September 16, 2025 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart with Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler present and approximately 100 people in the audience. Recognitions filled the opening: the 2025-2026 high school student representatives, spring 2025 all-state athletes, an all-girls robotics team named Global Team of the Year, and ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the year ending June 30, 2024. The most consequential action was unanimous acceptance of the administration's Attendance Area Review recommendation, approving boundary modifications effective beginning in the 2026/2027 school year.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, September 16, 2025, Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Called to order at 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart; adjourned at 9:34 p.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary.

**Attendance**
Present: Dr. Philippart plus Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler; Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Pagel, Jansen, Griffor, Trudel, and Milanov. Approximately 100 members of the audience. Every recorded vote was Yes 7, No 0.

**Recognitions**
- 2025-2026 student representatives: Chloe Gentilini (Troy College & Career High School), Ahyoung Song (International Academy-East), Sara Graunstadt (Athens High School), Isabella "Bella" Doss (Troy High School).
- Spring 2025 all-state athletes: Ashley Miller, Lauren DeJonckheere, Julian Farrell, Myles Linden, Katie Malon (Athens); Chase Duncan, Jason Hamilton, Olivia Jasniewicz (Troy High).
- Mission Moment: the district's first all-girls robotics team, founded December 2022, named Global Team of the Year; Coach Judy Bunao introduced the team.
- Student Spotlight: Creative Guild podcasters Sohyeon An (Smith) and Sidthbhiphob Suriwong (Larson), presented by Thomas Butcher.
- ASBO International Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024, credited to Dan Trudel, Aurel Malutan, and the Finance Team.

**Proclamation**
At the request of Oakland Community Health Network, the Board adopted a proclamation recognizing September 2025 as National Suicide Prevention Month (Anne / Alic). It cites World Suicide Prevention Day on September 10, the CDC figure of more than 48,000 deaths by suicide each year, and suicide as the second leading cause of death for people 10 to 34 years of age. Adopted 7-0.

**Consent Agenda and Personnel**
Items A and B approved (Haupt / Alic): minutes of the August 19, 2025 Special Board of Education Meeting and the Treasurer's Report for July 2025. John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on hiring drivers - retirements/resignations, leaves of absence, FTE status, enrollment - and noted the District hired 31 new teachers this year. Personnel recommendations approved (Alic / Anne). Curriculum: none.

**Business Actions**

| Item | Amount | Fund | Motion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Administration Building renovation | $1,560,680.30 | Capital Projects Fund | Haupt / Alic |
| Entrance ceiling soffits | $373,127.00 | Building Site and Sinking Fund | Haupt / Anne |
| Operable partition walls, Hamilton and Wass - Gardiner Vose, Inc. | $111,955.00 | Building Site and Sinking Fund | Anne / Haupt |

Dan Trudel gave a Bond Showcase Report with a PowerPoint of project photographs and statuses, covering Athens High School, Boulan Park Middle School, and elementary updates.

**Other Business**
- MASB 2025 Delegate Assembly, October 23 at 7:00 p.m.: Emina Alic, Audra Melton, Stephanie Zendler certified as delegates; Ayesha Potts alternate (Alic / Anne).
- 2026 NSBA Advocacy Institute, Washington, D.C., February 1-3, 2026: no more than two Board members (Potts / Haupt).
- 2026 NSBA Annual Conference for Public Education Leaders, San Antonio, Texas, April 10-12, 2026: no more than four Board members (Melton / Zendler).
- Attendance Area Review: Dr. Machesky presented the AARC recommendation; the Board approved the modifications effective beginning in the 2026/2027 school year (Melton / Haupt).

**Public Comment and Announcements**
One community member spoke on agenda items and one on non-agenda items; no action taken. The student representatives reported on school activities. Board comment topics: the cell phone policy, the Oakland County Government Relations Network Meeting, bond funds, the MASA Conference, the BOE Community Conversation on September 25 at 5:30 pm, no state budget yet, National School Attendance Month, TYA Magic of Hope, and the September 24 Business Roundtable. Next Board Workshop: October 7 at 6:00 p.m.; next regular meeting: October 14 at 7:00 p.m., Services Building.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
**Document and setting**
Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held September 16, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present, along with Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Pagel, Jansen, Griffor, Trudel, and Milanov. Approximately 100 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 9:34 p.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary (EA/jh).

**Student representatives to the Board, 2025-2026**
Chloe Gentilini, Troy College & Career High School: senior, student council and prom committee member, school store staff member, varsity student athlete, and a leader of Women of the Tomorrow; involved in Adopt a Family and Operation Blue Slay.
Ahyoung Song, International Academy-East: junior pursuing an IB diploma; captain of Science Olympiad, co-president of Science Fair, president of the Southeast and East Asian Student Association; leads the districtwide Math Pentathlon program across 3 elementary schools, coaching over 100 students at Costello and Hamilton Elementary schools; has presented research at the Michigan Science Fair and the International Science and Engineering Fair.
Sara Graunstadt, Athens High School: senior, Drum Major of the Athens Marching Band and flute player, member of the three-time state champion Athens powerlifting team; plans a career in pediatric speech-language pathology.
Isabella "Bella" Doss, Troy High School: senior, Vice President of the Student Government and Leadership Executive Board, Communications Director on the Troy High Model UN Executive Board, member of DECA and LEAP, representative of Troy High and Oakland County in the Michigan Association of Student Councils and Honor Societies (MASC/MAHS), and Chair of the Board's DEI Committee; spent two years on the Troy High School Drumline; plans to study business on the pre-law track.

**All-State Athletes - 2025 Spring Sports**
Mr. Jansen and the Board recognized: Ashley Miller, senior, Athens, girls' soccer; Lauren DeJonckheere, senior, Athens, girls' soccer; Julian Farrell, senior, Athens, boys' track; Myles Linden, senior, Athens, boys' track; Katie Malon, junior, Athens, girls' lacrosse; Chase Duncan, senior, Troy High, girls' lacrosse; Jason Hamilton, senior, Troy High, boys' track; Olivia Jasniewicz, junior, Troy High, girls' soccer.

**Mission Moment: all-girls robotics team, Global Team of the Year**
The Board featured the district's first all-girls robotics team as the September Mission Moment. Founded in December 2022, the team was named Global Team of the Year at an international tournament where it also led a global workshop. Coach Judy Bunao introduced the team. 2025-2026 season members: Jianna Cruz, Haneul Kim, Varna Jayaraman, Merrill Sanchez, Aarohi Sonar, Keerthana Chandra, Anwitha Vemuri. Youth mentors: Ella Bunao, Christel Jebu Mathew, Emmelyn Lauder, Gargi Sonawane, Sophia Alexander, Lauren Sanchez. Coaches and founders: Judy Bunao (Founder & Coach), Ed Bunao (Founder & Coach), Varun Jayaraman (Coach).

**Student Spotlight**
The first Student Spotlight of the year recognized Creative Guild students Sohyeon An, an 8th grader at Smith, and Sidthbhiphob Suriwong, an 8th grader at Larson, collaborators on a podcast project. Thomas Butcher shared their accomplishments.

**National Suicide Prevention Month proclamation**
Oakland Community Health Network (OCHN) asked school boards throughout Oakland County to approve a proclamation for September as National Suicide Prevention Month. Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mrs. Alic. The whereas clauses note that World Suicide Prevention Day is observed each year on September 10; that suicidal thoughts can affect anyone regardless of age, gender, race, orientation, income level, religion, or background; that according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) each year more than 48,000 people died by suicide; that suicide is the second leading cause of death for people 10 to 34 years of age, the fourth leading cause among people 35 to 54 years of age, and the eighth leading cause among people 55 to 64 years of age; that the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) and the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline, 988, help individuals in crisis; and that OCHN is committed to being a Zero Suicide organization. The resolution has OCHN recognize September 2025 as National Suicide Prevention Month and calls upon government agencies, public and private institutions, businesses, faith-based organizations, and schools to increase awareness of suicide prevention. Vote: Yes 7, No 0. Resolution adopted.

**ASBO Excellence in Financial Reporting for FY2024**
Dr. Philippart recognized the Business Office team for again receiving the ASBO Award. The Association of School Business Officials (ASBO) International awarded the Troy School District its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024, for a high-quality Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR). Credited were Assistant Superintendent of Business Services Dan Trudel, Finance Director Aurel Malutan, and the TSD Finance Team.

**Additions and deletions; public communication**
Additions and deletions: none. One community member addressed the Board on agenda items; no action was taken.

**Consent agenda**
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, the Board approved items A and B: minutes of the August 19, 2025 Special Board of Education Meeting, and the Treasurer's Report - July 2025. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Personnel - staffing update and new hires**
John Pagel, Assistant Superintendent for Employee Services, reported on the District's hiring process and the factors influencing the number of teachers hired each year, including retirements/resignations, full-year leaves of absence, FTE status, and student enrollment. This year the District hired 31 new teachers.
Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board approved the personnel recommendations. New hires: Heraldo Henrique Anjos Hatton, Caryn Baird, Alexandra Balcoff, Shawn Boucke, Julia Choi, Emily Conley, Dillon Coulter, Amy Dzapo, Bailey Fahnestock, Kenedi Harmon, Emma Hauberg, Erika Head, Jennifer Holdstock, Olivia Horrigan, Michael Jennings, Colin Johnson, Erica Johnson-Veggian, Crissy Karaszewski, Amanda Kovacs, Jennifer Liddell, Jessica Lovelace, Amy Macintosh, Mackenzie Maher, Grace Merriman, Abigail Minor, Neal Mozdzierz, Delaney O'Dell, Timothy Paccione, Shreya Patel, Julia Plesz, Erin Prendergast, Tex Profitt, Dana Reimann, Zoe Rosario, Jason Rose, Lauren Rouff, Kylie Schmehl, Tara Sheridan, Victoria Smirnov, Luke Telder, Heather Temrowski, Allison Van Buhler, Adrienne Weston, Anna Wilner. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Curriculum**
None.

**Business - construction and facilities bids**
Administration Building Renovation: moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, the bid was awarded as attached in the amount of $1,560,680.30, approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund, with the renovation awarded to the vendors listed in the attachment. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
Elementary Soffit Replacement Project: moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Anne, the bid for the purchase and installation of entrance ceiling soffits was awarded as attached in the amount of $373,127.00, approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
Hamilton & Wass Operable Wall Replacement: moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mr. Haupt, the bid for operable partition walls for Hamilton and Wass Elementaries was awarded to Gardiner Vose, Inc. in the amount of $111,955.00, approved as an expenditure of the Building Site and Sinking Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Bond Showcase Report**
Assistant Superintendent Dan Trudel gave a brief report updating the Board and community on bond projects throughout the District, sharing a PowerPoint presentation with photographs and the status of each project. He discussed upcoming projects and construction of Athens High School, Boulan Park Middle School, and elementary updates.

**Public communication (non-agenda items) and student reports**
One community member addressed the Board; no action was taken. Chloe Gentilini, Ahyoung Song, Sara Graunstadt, and Isabella (Bella) Doss each reported on events and activities at their schools.

**Other - conference and assembly representation**
MASB 2025 Delegate Assembly: moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Anne, the Board certified Emina Alic, Audra Melton, and Stephanie Zendler as delegates to the MASB 2025 Delegate Assembly on October 23 at 7:00 p.m., with Ayesha Potts as alternate. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
NSBA Advocacy Institute 2026, Washington, D.C., February 1 - 3, 2026: moved by Mrs. Potts, supported by Mr. Haupt, the Board approved a delegation of no more than two (2) Board members. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.
NSBA 2026 Annual Conference for Public Education Leaders, San Antonio, Texas, April 10 - 12, 2026: moved by Dr. Melton, supported by Mrs. Zendler, the Board approved a delegation of no more than four (4) Board members. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**AARC recommendation and acceptance**
Dr. Machesky shared administration's recommendation for the Attendance Area Review project, with a brief history of the AARC process and the reasoning behind it. Moved by Dr. Melton, supported by Mr. Haupt, the resolution recites the need for periodic review of attendance areas to maintain balanced enrollment, maximize effective use of district facilities, and support students' academic, social, and emotional needs, and the administration's analysis of enrollment data, projected student population trends, and facility capacities, plus stakeholder engagement through public meetings, surveys, and other outreach. The Board approved the recommended modifications as provided, effective beginning in the 2026/2027 school year, and directed the Superintendent and administrative team to implement the changes as presented. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Board comments and announcements**
Board members welcomed new staff and everyone back to the new school year, mentioning: the cell phone policy and restrictions in schools; the Oakland County Government Relations Network Meeting; bond funds; the MASA Conference; the BOE Community Conversation on September 25 at 5:30 pm; fall updates to building staff and PTOs beginning in October; curriculum nights; no state budget yet, with the community urged to write to legislators; National School Attendance Month; TYA Magic of Hope; and the Business Roundtable on September 24th. Dr. Philippart announced the next Board Workshop in the Administration Building on October 7th at 6:00 p.m. and the next regular meeting on October 14th in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: Award packet documenting that the Association of School Business Officials International (ASBO) granted Troy School District its Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024. The packet contains the certificate, a June 18, 2025 congratulatory letter to Assistant Superintendent of Business Services Daniel Trudel, an ASBO press release, and the review team's comments dated June 16, 2025. The review team awarded the certificate by consensus and issued a single improvement comment about analysis of individual major capital projects funds.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
**The award**
ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting is presented to Troy School District for its Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2024. The certificate states that the district report meets the criteria established for the award and is signed by Ryan S. Stechschulte, President, and James M. Rowan, CAE, SFO, CEO/Executive Director.

**Notification letter**
Dated June 18, 2025 and addressed to Daniel Trudel, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Rd, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777. Signed by James M. Rowan, CEO/Executive Director. The letter encourages use of the COE recipient's logo in emails and marketing materials, and instructs the district to review and address the review team's comments before preparing next year's report; a copy of the original comments and the district's written responses must be included in next year's application packet. A press release and the award certificate were attached.

**Press release**
For immediate release from Reston, VA, dated June 18, 2025; media contact Allison Barton-Kramer, abarton-kramer@asbointl.org. The release quotes Jim Rowan, CAE, SFO, Executive Director: "For over half a century, ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting has been the gold standard for promoting and recognizing excellence in financial transparency." It notes that submitted ACFRs are reviewed by a panel of experienced financial professionals and that the distinction supports bond rating and continuing bond disclosure processes. The program is sponsored by Strategic Partner American Fidelity; more information at asbointl.org/COE. ASBO International was established in 1910 and unites a global network of approximately 30,000 school business professionals.

**Review comments**
Dated June 16, 2025 for Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024. The review team reached consensus to award the Certificate of Excellence, commended the district for its efforts, and described the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report as being of high quality. One comment was issued, referencing page 7: include analysis of significant balances and transactions of the individual major funds (capital projects), citing eGAAFR chapter 31, page 606.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
Board packet material presenting Troy School District's receipt of the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting from the Association of School Business Officials International (ASBO), together with the underlying correspondence, press release and review-team comments.

CERTIFICATE. The certificate reads that the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting is presented to Troy School District for its Annual Comprehensive Financial Report for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2024, and that the district report meets the criteria established for ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting. It carries the signatures of Ryan S. Stechschulte, President, and James M. Rowan, CAE, SFO, CEO/Executive Director.

NOTIFICATION LETTER. Dated June 18, 2025, the letter is addressed to Daniel Trudel, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, Troy School District, 4400 Livernois Rd, Troy, Michigan 48098-4777, and opens "Dear Daniel." Writing on behalf of ASBO, James M. Rowan informs the district that Troy School District has received ASBO's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, characterizing the award as a significant achievement that reflects the district's commitment to transparency and high-quality financial reporting. The letter encourages the district to use the COE recipient's logo to share the achievement in emails and marketing materials. It states that the Certificate of Excellence (COE) Review Team has provided comments for the improvement of the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, that it is important to review the comments and address them before preparing next year's report, and that the district must include a copy of the original comments and the district's written responses to those comments in next year's application packet. A press release for sharing the achievement with the community and the award certificate were attached. The letter closes with congratulations to Trudel and the staff members who worked to earn the COE and an expression of interest in the district's continued participation in the COE program.

PRESS RELEASE. Marked FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE, with contact Allison Barton-Kramer at abarton-kramer@asbointl.org, and datelined Reston, VA - June 18, 2025. Headlined "Troy School District Honored with ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting," the release announces that Troy School District (Michigan) has been awarded the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting (COE), an honor that recognizes school districts upholding the highest standards of financial reporting and transparency. The district earned the certificate for its Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR) for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2024. Jim Rowan, CAE, SFO, Executive Director of ASBO International, is quoted: "For over half a century, ASBO International's Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting has been the gold standard for promoting and recognizing excellence in financial transparency. Clear and accurate financial reporting is crucial for engaging school communities and building their trust. Districts that earn the COE have demonstrated an extraordinary commitment to these principles." The release explains that participation in the COE program highlights a district's dedication to financial accountability, that submitted ACFRs are rigorously reviewed by a panel of experienced financial professionals who provide constructive feedback to enhance the quality of future reports, and that districts meeting the program's stringent requirements are awarded the Certificate of Excellence - a distinction that also supports bond rating and continuing bond disclosure processes. The program is proudly sponsored by Strategic Partner American Fidelity, and readers are directed to asbointl.org/COE.

ABOUT THE ORGANIZATIONS. The release notes that ASBO International was established in 1910 and is a nonprofit organization that unites, through its members and affiliates, a global network of approximately 30,000 school business professionals, empowering members with programs, resources and connections intended to set the standard for excellence in school business management; more information at asbointl.org. A companion section on American Fidelity describes the company as familiar with the education community, functioning as an extension of a district's HR department, administering the entire benefits program, educating employees through in-person education and customized communications, providing an enrollment platform for benefits enrollment, and helping keep the district and its program compliant.

REVIEW COMMENTS. Dated June 16, 2025, the Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting Review Comments are addressed to Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, for the Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2024. The document states that it is the consensus of the review team to award the Certificate of Excellence, that the District is to be commended for its efforts, and that the Annual Comprehensive Financial Report is of high quality. Under the FINANCIAL SECTION heading, one comment is listed at reference page 7, item 1: include analysis of significant balances and transactions of the individual major funds (capital projects), with a citation to eGAAFR chapter 31, page 606.

GASB UPDATES. Provided as a courtesy, the review comments list the Governmental Accounting Standards Board statements the district should consider, as applicable, in preparing future Annual Comprehensive Financial Reports. GASB Statement No. 101, Compensated Absences, issued June 2022, updates the recognition and measurement guidance for compensated absences by aligning that guidance under a unified model and amending certain previously required disclosures; its requirements are effective for periods beginning after December 15, 2023. GASB Statement No. 102, Certain Risk Disclosures, issued December 2023, establishes financial reporting requirements for risks related to vulnerabilities due to certain concentrations or constraints; effective for periods beginning after June 15, 2024. GASB Statement No. 103, Financial Reporting Model Improvements, issued April 2024, improves key components of the financial reporting model to enhance its effectiveness in providing information essential for decision-making and assessing a government's accountability, and addresses certain application issues; effective for periods beginning after June 15, 2025. GASB Statement No. 104, Disclosure of Certain Capital Assets, issued September 2024, provides users of financial statements with essential information about certain types of capital assets in order to make informed decisions and assess accountability; effective for periods beginning after June 15, 2025. The comment document carries ASBO International's address, 11160 C-1 South Lakes Drive, #808, Reston, VA 20191, and phone 866.682.2729.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held July 15, 2025 at the Troy School District Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, called to order by President Philippart at 9:35 a.m. and adjourned at 10:18 a.m. The board approved consent agenda items A through G and then took three personnel actions: extending administrator contracts through June 30, 2026, extending the four assistant superintendents through June 30, 2027, and extending Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's contract to run July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2030. Each vote was recorded as 6 yes, 0 no, with Zendler noted as absent/remote. The board released an evaluation describing Dr. Machesky as an exemplary superintendent.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
Meeting
Board of Education, Troy, Michigan. Regular board meeting, July 15, 2025, held at the Troy School District Administration Building, 4400 Livernois. Called to order by President Philippart at 9:35 a.m.; adjourned at 10:18 a.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education (notation EA/jh).

Attendance
Present: Dr. Philippart plus Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton and Potts. Mrs. Zendler attended via remote communications. Also present: Superintendent Machesky; administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Trudel and Pagel; and two members of the audience. Recognition, additions and deletions, and public communication were all recorded as none.

Consent Agenda
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Anne, to approve items A through G: minutes of the June 3, 2025 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the June 3, 2025 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the June 3, 2025 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the June 17, 2025 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for May 2025; settlement terms of Batista v Office of Retirement Services litigation; and rescheduling of the October 21st Board of Education Meeting and the December 2nd and January 6th Board Workshops. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Personnel — Administrator Contract Extensions
Moved by Mrs. Anne, supported by Mrs. Alic, to extend the contracts of the listed administrators through June 30, 2026, or as otherwise indicated in the administrator's individual contract, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook where applicable and as permitted by law. The list covered high school principals (Vernon Burden, Patrick Griffin, Remo Roncone), middle school principals (Ryan Brinks, Jonathan Cross, Anthony Morse, Brian Zawislak), eleven elementary principals, nine assistant principals, and five directors/supervisors. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Assistant Superintendent Contracts
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic, to extend the contracts of Dan Trudel (Business Services), John Pagel (Employee Services), Kris Griffor (Elementary Instruction) and Christine DiPilato (Secondary Instruction) through June 30, 2027, without tenure in the administrative positions. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Superintendent Evaluation and Contract
The board reported completing Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation and shared an assessment rating him EXEMPLARY, having met or exceeded expectations in all evaluation categories. Points cited: continued execution of the strategic plan under the LEARNING FOR ALL vision; fiscal strength with sufficient fund balance to mitigate disruptions in state funding; a new business operations team integrated this year; bond projects tracking at or below budget; alignment and implementation of Multi-Tiered System of Support; new secondary assessments; math and literacy professional development; belonging, well-being and security initiatives; and all staff labor agreements negotiated and signed. The board committed to a more robust community-input process in curriculum evaluation and praised the Career Accelerator Program, run with the Business Roundtable, which provided 75 high school students with internships in local businesses. The minutes note that Dr. Machesky's contract then ran through June 30, 2029 and that the board planned to extend it by an additional year. Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Mrs. Anne, the extension was approved to be in effect July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2030, without tenure and subject to the provisions of the written Agreement. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent/Remote Zendler.

Other
Curriculum and Business items: none. Public communication on non-agenda items: none. Other items noted: summer work progress update, Data Dashboard update, and the MASB Conference in October. Dr. Philippart announced the next Board of Education meeting for August 19th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building.

CONSENT AGENDA

PERSONNEL — EXTENSION OF ADMINISTRATIVE PERSONNEL CONTRACTS
It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Troy Board of Education approve the extension of the contracts of the named administrators through June 30, 2026, or as otherwise indicated in the administrator's individual contract, without tenure in the administrative positions and subject to the layoff provision in the Administrative Handbook, where applicable and as permitted by law.

The vote was recorded as Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent/Remote: Zendler.

SUPERINTENDENT EVALUATION
The minutes record that the Board recently completed Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky's performance evaluation and shared the resulting assessment with the community. The assessment states that Dr. Machesky is an EXEMPLARY superintendent who has met or exceeded expectations in all evaluation categories. It credits him with continuing to execute the district's strategic plan and driving high expectations for the vision of LEARNING FOR ALL as the basis for instructional decisions. It states the district remains fiscally strong under his leadership with sufficient fund balance to mitigate disruptions in state funding, that a new business operations team was integrated into the organization during the year, and that bond projects are tracking at or below budget. The district continues to focus on alignment and implementation of Multi-Tiered System of Support to address achievement gaps, particularly for special education students, English Language Learners and economically disadvantaged students. New assessments were put in place for secondary students to identify achievement gaps, and high-quality teacher professional development in math and literacy was provided for all grade levels. Several initiatives were put in place to increase students' sense of belonging, well-being and security. All staff labor agreements were successfully negotiated and signed during the year, providing the district with attractive compensation to retain and recruit staff. Going forward, Dr. Machesky and the board committed to developing a more robust process that gathers input and engages the community earlier in the curriculum evaluation process while still relying on the expertise of the district's educators for decision-making. The board also applauded Rich and the Business Roundtable for implementation of a growing, successful Career Accelerator Program that provided 75 high school students with internship opportunities in local businesses. The board expressed full confidence that he and his team have the capacity and capability to face future challenges.

EXTENSION OF SUPERINTENDENT CONTRACT
The minutes note that Dr. Machesky's contract at that time ran through June 30, 2029 and that the board planned to extend it by an additional year. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the Troy Board of Education extend the contract of the Superintendent of Schools as described, with the contract to be in effect from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2030, without tenure in the administrative position and subject to provisions of the written Agreement. The vote was recorded as Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent/Remote: Zendler.

CURRICULUM, BUSINESS AND PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
No curriculum or business action items were recorded; the entries for these sections and for public communication on non-agenda items are marked none.

OTHER AND BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS
Items noted under other business and board member comments: a summer work progress update, a Data Dashboard update, and the MASB Conference in October.

ADJOURNMENT
Dr. Philippart shared that the next Board of Education Meeting would be held on August 19th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building. The meeting was adjourned at 10:18 a.m. Respectfully submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education; typist notation EA/jh.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, June 17, 2025, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Called to order by President Philippart at 7:02 p.m.; adjourned at 8:58 p.m. Approximately 150 members of the audience attended.

**Attendance**
Present: Dr. Philippart plus Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Pagel, Griffor, Haezebrouck, Recker, Detmer, Singh, Cross, and Trudel.

**Public Hearing - 2025/2026 Proposed Budget**
Mr. Trudel presented the proposed budget to the Board and community with a PowerPoint, noting the budget had been reviewed in detail with the Board at the June workshop. He covered tax values, homestead/non-homestead millage, general fund adjustments and assumptions, ancillary funds, the sinking fund and capital projects fund, student enrollment, foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board indicated it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 3rd Workshop. One community member asked for clarification on what sinking funds are and how they are used.

**Recognitions**
- TSD Mission Moment: Ava Bunao, Athens High School graduate, runner up for the 2025 Gold Award Girl Scout Young Women of Distinction for her project "On the Spot Community First Aid Awareness for Outdoor Recreation," and recipient of the GSUSA Gold Award Scholarship given to one Gold Award Girl Scout per council. She will attend Michigan State University as a biochemistry major.
- TSD Mission Moment: the Bemis Math Pentathlon team, winners of the 2025 National Math Pentathlon First Place Gold Trophy, introduced by Bemis Principal Mrs. Harleen Singh.
- Student Spotlight: TSD Creative Guild graduates Akshaya Rachamadugu (2025 Troy High) and Anoush Rophael (2025 Athens), presented by Mr. Thomas Butcher.

**Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage**
Moved by Mrs. Zendler, supported by Mrs. Anne. Whereas clauses cite that firearm-related deaths are the leading cause of death among children and adolescents; that firearm death rates among ages 14 to 17 are 22.5% higher than motor vehicle-related death rates; that 76% of school-grounds attackers acquired a firearm from the home of a parent or close relative per a US Secret Service report; that roughly 350 children under 18 unintentionally shoot themselves or someone else each year; that nearly 22,000 Americans die by firearm suicide annually including over 950 children and teens; and that 47% of firearm owners with children at home do not safely store at least one weapon. The resolution directs the Superintendent to communicate the importance of safe firearm storage during gun violence awareness month and to include secure-storage material in annual notification materials. Adopted Yes 7, No 0, certified by Secretary Emina Alic under the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976.

**Meeting identification.** Minutes of a regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held June 17, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Pagel, Griffor, Haezebrouck, Recker, Detmer, Singh, Cross, and Trudel. Approximately 150 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 8:58 p.m. The minutes are submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carry the typist notation EA/jh.

**Public hearing on the 2025/2026 proposed budget.** The business portion opened with a public hearing on the proposed 2025/2026 budget. Mr. Trudel presented the details of the proposed budget to the Board and community and shared a PowerPoint presentation. He noted the proposed budget had been reviewed in great detail with the Board at the June workshop. His presentation addressed tax values, homestead and non-homestead millage, general fund adjustments and assumptions, ancillary funds, the sinking fund, and the capital projects fund. He also reviewed student enrollment, the District's foundation allowance history, and revenues and expenditures. The Board indicated it had reviewed the proposed budget in its entirety at the June 3rd Workshop. President Philippart invited questions from the audience related to the proposed budget; one question was asked by a community member to clarify what the sinking funds are and how they are used.

**Recognition: Ava Bunao.** The Board recognized recent graduate Ava Bunao, named a runner up for the 2025 Gold Award Girl Scout Young Women of Distinction for her project "On the Spot Community First Aid Awareness for Outdoor Recreation." The project focused on providing access to first aid resources in local outdoor recreation areas and on teaching community members how to use them. It also earned the GSUSA Gold Award Scholarship, which is awarded to one Gold Award Girl Scout per council. Ava graduated from Athens High School with high honors and numerous scholarships and will begin college at Michigan State University as a biochemistry major and a student in the Osteopathic Medical Scholars Program on a pre-medicine track. She was invited to the podium to describe her Gold Award project.

**Recognition: Bemis Math Pentathlon team.** A second Mission Moment honored the Bemis Math Pentathlon team for earning the 2025 National Math Pentathlon First Place Gold Trophy. Mrs. Harleen Singh, Principal of Bemis, came to the podium to describe the achievement and introduce the champion team. The following students received a certificate of achievement and congratulations from Board members: Aashvi Vatsa, Aiden Rajbhandari, Anika Gollamudi, Aryian Majjhoo, Elias Roumayah, Ishan Vankadara, Shardul Joshi, Vihaan Palepu, Atharv Salimath, Ayona Chauhan, Bhashith Thulugu, Mannat Thakur, Navneeth Sheshathri, Ryka Kashi, Sanvika GopalaKrishnan, Sarah Farah, Vihaa Chethan, Alexander Majjhoo, Aniket Pagi, Ayla Majjhoo, Cali Hoskins, Charles Carlisle, Dhruhi Bhatt, Eleanor Roumayah, Feruz Mamarasulov, Gourika Kurkimatt, Grace Thomas, Irene Thommana, Naaga Nainika Dhavala, Nainika Chowdhury, Nate Zhang, Prarthana Gowda, Srihith Gattupalli, Varun Prasanth Kumar, Anushka Sonar, Asha Thabolingam, Bruno Redondo, Fatima Bilal, Hari Kern, Kaira Singh, Ritwika Thanigaivel, Saisha Fegade, Tiyasa Giri, Adam Majjhoo, Anirudh Ganesh, Isaac Thommana, Padmesh Lekkala Haribabu, Pugal Suresh Babu, Rayan Pedaballe, Shrivatsav Santapuri, Dheeya Gopalakrishnan, Satyapavana Gattupalli, Shilpa Manni, and Varnika Prasanth Kumar.

**Student Spotlight.** The Student Spotlight recognized creative achievement in the TSD Creative Guild, described at this meeting as more accurately an Alumni Spotlight. Recent graduates Akshaya Rachamadugu (2025 Troy High graduate) and Anoush Rophael (2025 Athens graduate) were recognized for dedication to Creative Guild throughout their high school careers. Mr. Thomas Butcher was invited up to share the achievement.

**Resolution in Support of Gun Safety and Safe Gun Storage.** Moved by Mrs. Zendler and supported by Mrs. Anne. The whereas clauses state that the safety and well-being of students, teachers, and staff is a top priority in the Troy School District; that firearm-related deaths are the leading cause of death among children and adolescents; that rates of death from firearms among ages 14 to 17 are now 22.5% higher than motor vehicle-related death rates, and that in the U.S. middle and high school age children are now more likely to die as the result of a firearm injury than from any other single cause of death; that according to a report from the US Secret Service, in incidents of gun violence on school grounds 76% of attackers acquired a firearm from the home of a parent or another close relative; that every year roughly 350 children under the age of 18 unintentionally shoot themselves or someone else; that nearly 22,000 Americans die by firearm suicide every year, including over 950 children and teens; that research indicates 47% of firearm owners who have children living in their homes do not safely store at least one of their weapons; that evidence strongly suggests secure firearm storage is an essential component of any effective community safety strategy; that keeping students, teachers and staff safe from the threat of gun violence should be the responsibility of all adult stakeholders in the district; and that preventative measures require action now.

The resolving clauses direct the Superintendent to periodically communicate the importance of safe firearm storage and other firearm safety and violence prevention measures during gun violence awareness month, and to disseminate material on an annual basis stressing the importance of secure storage of firearms by including it in the District's annual notification materials. A further clause commits the Board and Superintendent to continue working with local law enforcement agencies, medical and mental health agencies, and non-profit organizations to increase efforts to inform District parents of their obligations regarding secure storage of firearms in their homes and other gun violence prevention safety measures. A final clause provides that the resolution shall not be construed to conflict with any existing Michigan or federal law. The vote was Yes 7, No 0, and the resolution was declared adopted. Emina Alic, Secretary, Board of Education, certified the resolution as a true and complete copy duly adopted at a regular meeting held on the 17th day of June, 2025, with notice given in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976. Citations appended to the resolution reference news.umich.edu, labblog.uofmhealth.org, the US Secret Service publication Protecting America's Schools, Everytown Research's "Not an Accident" map and its report on the rise of firearm suicide among young Americans, a Pew Research Center guns report, and David C. Grossman et al., "Gun Storage Practices and Risk of Youth Suicide and Unintentional Firearm Injuries," JAMA 293, no. 6 (2005): 707-14.

**Additions and deletions; agenda-item public communication.** None recorded for either.

**Personnel.** Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Board issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Ms. Ebert, who will begin her duties as Assistant Principal, Baker Middle School commencing with the 2025-26 school year. Moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Potts that the Board issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure to Dr. David Recker, who will begin his duties as Director, Teaching & Learning commencing with the 2025-26 school year. **Curriculum: Elementary Writing Units of Study.** The Director of Teaching and Learning, with members of the Teaching & Learning team, provided information to Board members on recommended materials for grades K-5 for the upcoming school year; Board members had reviewed the plan and asked questions following the Board Workshop. Moved by Mrs. Potts and supported by Mrs. Alic that the recommended materials for grades K-5 be approved starting in the 2025-2026 school year. Mrs. Zendler shared a statement informing the community and fellow board members that she would be voting no on the proposed writing curriculum. Dr. Melton shared that upon further research and investigation she would not support the adoption. **Business: Smith Middle School EPIC system.** Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the purchase of an EPIC system for Smith Middle School be approved through VSC Inc. in the amount of $173,978.00, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, May 20, 2025, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Vice President Anne presided for President Philippart, who was not in attendance, and called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m.; adjourned at 8:54 p.m. Approximately 200 members of the audience attended.

**Attendance**
Present with Mrs. Anne: Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler, plus Superintendent Machesky and administrators including Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Keyser, Brennan, Cottone, Barsh, Crowe, Haezebrouck, Smotherman, Burdette, Pagel, and Trudel.

**Recognitions**
- 2025 Outstanding Support Person of the Year: Phyllis Walters, Administrative Assistant to the Principal at Wass Elementary School, chosen from 24 nominees and nominated by the entire Wass staff. Her name was engraved on the Support Person Plaque to be displayed at her building for the next year, and she received a check for $250 from the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence. Principal Kristin Crowe accepted the plaque on her behalf.
- Retirees: Mr. Pagel read the name and District tenure of each employee who retired or intends to retire at the end of the 2024-2025 school year, a group with start years running from 1974 to 2024.
- TSD Mission Moment: the Troy Athens girls' powerlifting team, 2025 State Champions and winners of a third consecutive state title, recognized with certificates.

| Resolution | Mover / Support | Vote |
|---|---|---|
| National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 5-9, 2025 | Alic / Haupt | 6-0, Philippart absent |
| Mental Health Awareness Month, May 2025 | Melton / Potts | 6-0, Philippart absent |

**Consent Agenda (items A through K), moved by Haupt, supported by Alic, 6-0**
Minutes of the April 1, 2025 Workshop; minutes of the April 22, 2025 Special Board Meeting & Closed Session; minutes of the April 22, 2025 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report for March 2025; Approve Oakland Intermediate School District Budget; Resolution to Hold a Public Hearing on the Proposed 2025/2026 School Year Budget; IA Budget Approval for 2024/2025 School Year; OCSBA Amendment to Bylaws; Troy High Kitchen Upgrades; Transportation Parking Lot Lighting; and Beverage Cooler Replacement - Baker MS.

**Meeting identification.** Minutes of a regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held May 20, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Vice President Anne presided for President Philippart, who was not in attendance, and called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. In addition to Mrs. Anne, Board members Alic, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Keyser, Brennan, Cottone, Barsh, Crowe, Haezebrouck, Smotherman, Burdette, Jansen, Roncone, Brinks, House, Hall, Keen, Detmer, DiPonio, Harker, Pagel, and Trudel. Approximately 200 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 8:54 p.m. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation EA/jh.

**Recognition: 2025 Outstanding Support Staff Award.** The Board recognized the District's Outstanding Support Person of the Year, a category covering bus drivers, secretaries, paraprofessionals, student support aides, custodial staff, food service, technology, childcare, security, and more. There were 24 nominees this year. The 2025 honoree is Phyllis Walters, Administrative Assistant to the Principal at Wass Elementary School, nominated by the entire Wass staff. Nomination comments read into the record described her as a problem-solver who heads off problems before they can become one; extremely organized, efficient, trustworthy, and kind; going above and beyond for students and families every day; the reason Wass runs smoothly and the backbone of the school; and resilient, adaptable, with unwavering dedication. Her name was engraved on the Support Person Plaque that will be displayed at her building for the next year, and she was surprised with a check for $250 from the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence. A short video of the surprise visit was shared with the Board and audience. Principal Kristin Crowe was present to accept the plaque on Phyllis Walters' behalf, as she was unable to attend the meeting.

**Recognition: Troy School District retirees.** The Board recognized employees who retired or expressed their intention to retire at the end of the 2024-2025 school year. Mr. Pagel read each name with the length of the employee's District career: Ruba Alexander (Teacher, Troy Union, dedicated employee since 1995), Nadia Barbat (Teacher, Baker, since 2005), Michelle Barsh (Principal, Martell, since 2018), Heather Childress (Teacher, Martell, since 1998), Kelly Chlebek (Counselor, Baker, since 2004), Cindy Christiansen (Teacher, Larson, since 2007), Melissa Curth (Assistant Principal, Troy High, since 1995), Paula Davidson (Para-Professional, Wattles, since 2010), Carol Dospil (Teacher, Hamilton, since 1985), Laura Duzey (Central Enrollment/Pupil Accounting Coordinator, Central Office, since 1999), Erin Fischer-Ballew (Teacher, Troy High, since 2000), Rose Gavrilovska (Systems Analyst, Services, since 2024), Shelley Hakala (Teacher, Troy High, since 1999), Joe Havrilla (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1994), Jane Held (Teacher, Martell, since 2003), Robert Holder (Teacher, Athens, since 2000), Carrie Johnson (Teacher, Baker, since 1999), Patrick Koneval (Teacher, Smith, since 1991), Sandy Koneval (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1993), Frank Leone (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1981), Kathryn Loch (Teacher, Baker/Larson, since 2003), Diane Loucks (Teacher, Troy High, since 1995), Krista Manfredi (Teacher, Athens, since 1974), Benjamin Martin (Teacher, Wattles, since 2000), Cathy Matthes (Secretary, Barnard, since 1996), Shelley McHugh (Teacher, Larson, since 2002), Brenda Rice (Teacher, Athens, since 1996), Jennifer Sobczynski (Teacher, Troy High, since 1990), Linda Stanko (Early Childhood Coordinator, Preschool, since 1985), Jennifer Taylor (Teacher, Boulan Park, since 1986), Lori Ulewicz (Teacher, Baker, since 1989), Carolyn Van Noord (Project Search Instructor, Troy School District, since 2006), Marie Weber (Explorer Supervisor, Preschool, since 1999), and Mike DeSantis (Teacher, Athens, beloved employee since 1996).

**Recognition: Athens girls' powerlifting champions.** The Board celebrated the Troy Athens Powerlifting team as 2025 State Champions, noting the team secured its third consecutive state title while competing on national and global stages and shattering school, state, and national records. The following powerlifters came forward for a certificate and congratulations from the Board: Alessandra Alojipan, Julia Arnett, Lillian Flores, Mariana Gould, Sara Graunstadt, Mya Hangstebeck, Camilla Inadeski, Reemas Kaakarni, Lillian Kotila, Ciara Lenz, Indira Martinez, Cassidy Morse, Izzie Piotrowski, Addison Pokley, Erica Seidel, Kata Tasich, Luleta Thaqi, Mikayla Twum, and Emma Walters.

**Legislative CAP students report.** The Board welcomed students from the Legislative track of the District's Career Accelerator Program (CAP), who have been engaged in learning about levels of government from the school board and the city to state senators and representatives. Two students shared experiences, insights, and how CAP affected their educational journey. The students named were Aarav Akolkar (THS), Tanmayee Choudary Gudi (IAE), Jackson Kanczuzewski (AHS), Amarachi Obiakor (IAE), Melita Pereira (IAE), Naina Rodrigues (THS), Jyostsna Shivakumar (THS), Ragavarshini Venkatesh (THS), and Vinicius Zanta Leao da Silva (IAE).

**National Teacher Appreciation Week resolution.** Teacher Appreciation Week is observed nationally each May and was celebrated Monday, May 5th through Friday, May 9th this year. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt, the resolution recites that teachers inspire, nurture and open children's minds to new ideas; that teachers promote and strengthen the principles of democratic equality, develop leaders and encourage critical thinking; that Troy teachers set the bar for excellence in education and continually exceed the highest standards in the profession; and that the goal of Teacher Appreciation Week is to raise national and local awareness of teaching excellence in building a better society. It resolves that the Troy School District supports National Teacher Appreciation Week, May 5-9, 2025 and encourages schools and community to recognize the vital and changing role of teachers. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Mental Health Awareness Month resolution.** Each year Oakland Community Health Network and its service provider network host initiatives promoting community awareness about mental illness, and school boards across Oakland County were asked to recognize May as Mental Health Awareness Month. Moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mrs. Potts, the resolution recites that mental health is important for individual well-being and vitality as well as that of families, communities, and schools; that one in five of all Americans, including children, experience mental health issues that could lead to school difficulties, physical problems, and even suicide; and that May 8, 2025 is designated National Children's Mental Health Awareness Day and May 12 through May 18, 2025 is designated Children's Mental Health Acceptance Week. It resolves that the Troy Board of Education recognizes May 2025 as Mental Health Awareness Month and seeks to increase awareness and understanding of mental illness and the need to support all people seeking help. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Personnel.** Moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mrs. Zendler that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure in the administrative position to Colette Ivey, who will begin her duties as Principal, Martell Elementary School effective July 1, 2025. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Moved by Dr. Melton and supported by Mrs. Potts that the Board issue a two-year administrative contract without tenure to Mr. Ross Burdette, who will begin his duties as Principal, Hill Elementary School commencing with the 2025-26 school year. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mrs. Jesse Allgeier, who will begin her duties as Assistant Principal, Troy High School effective July 1, 2025. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart. Moved by Mrs. Potts and supported by Mrs. Zendler that the Board issue a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure to Mrs. Jamie Evans, who will begin her duties as Special Education Supervisor, Services Building effective July 1, 2025. Vote: Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Curriculum and Business.** No items were presented under either heading.

**Public communication and student representative reports.** Nine community members addressed the Board during public communication; no action was taken by the Board. Kristian Vitanovich, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, reported on events and activities at his school. Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, reported on events and activities at her school. Adam McManus, student representative for Troy High School, reported on events and activities at his school. Diana D'Aloisio, student representative for Athens High School, was not in attendance.

**Board member comments and sentiments.** Mrs. Alic shared sentiments about Boulan Park 8th grade student Bilal Ahmad, who passed away unexpectedly during Freshman Orientation at Troy High School on May 1st, and noted the family would hold a Celebration of Life to honor him. Other comments congratulated the retirees again; expressed appreciation for public comments regarding the writing curriculum; invited attendance at the June 3rd Workshop for information on PA146 legislation; thanked teachers for another great school year; gave a shout out to 2025 graduates, with ceremonies for THS and AHS on 5/31, IA on 6/1, and TCCHS on 6/4; announced the upcoming SSAB Leadership Conference 5/23, Open Air Fest 5/28, and TFEE Golf Outing 6/10; welcomed new administrators; and thanked all who helped with 8th Grade Interviews. Mrs. Anne announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, June 3rd at 6:00 p.m. at the Services Building and the next Board of Education Meeting for Tuesday, June 17th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: A 21-slide presentation by Kim St. Martin, Ph.D., Director of the MiMTSS Technical Assistance Center (mimtsstac.org), dated June 2025, walks the Troy Board of Education through Michigan's K-12 Literacy/Dyslexia Law. Public Acts 146 and 147 of 2024 were signed by Governor Whitmer on October 10, 2024; PA 146 revises the 1280f Read by Grade Three statute, extends Individual Reading Improvement Plans across K-3, mandates specified screening measures in K-3 and indicator-triggered screening in grades 4-12, and requires Tier 1 instruction to use a "code-emphasis instructional approach." MDE must update its approved assessment list and publish a list of evidence-based Tier 1 reading curricula and materials by January 1, 2026.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
**Presentation**: "PA 146 Legislative Overview," PowerPoint, 21 slides, presented to the Troy Board of Education, meeting date June 3, 2025.
**Presenter**: Kim St. Martin, Ph.D., Director, MiMTSS TA Center (mimtsstac.org). **Dated**: June 2025.

**Framing**
Bipartisan laws Public Act 146 and Public Act 147 of 2024 were signed by Governor Whitmer on October 10, 2024, to improve reading outcomes for K-12 learners, affecting in-service and pre-service teachers. They are frequently called the K-12 Literacy/Dyslexia Law. The law is not focused on diagnosing learners with dyslexia.

**PA 146 components**
PA 146 includes Read by Grade Three, revising the 1280f statute. Individual Reading Improvement Plans (IRIPs) span K-3; 4th grade IRIPs are NOT included, though MDE is examining K-12 language to clarify requirements beyond 3rd grade. IRIP information must be reported to ISDs de-identified, then aggregated and sent to MDE. Diagnostic assessments are no longer referenced, and the term "district-identified coaches" is infused into the language.

**Assessment requirements**

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held April 22, 2025 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Philippart at 7:02 p.m. and adjourned at 8:50 p.m. The Board honored the 2025 Outstanding Teachers of the Year, the Troy High Model United Nations team, Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit participants, district volunteers, and adopted a resolution recognizing April 2025 as Autism Acceptance Month. On the business agenda the Board approved by 7-0 votes a purchase of Apple iPads and cases for $846,202.50, a temporary fencing bid to Fence Connection for $56,282.00, and a Smith Middle School furniture pilot not to exceed $71,950.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, April 22, 2025, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.; adjournment at 8:50 p.m. Approximately 100 members of the audience attended. Minutes submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary (EA/jh).

**Attendance**
Board: Philippart, Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, Zendler. Administration: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Keyser, Brennan, Pagel, and Trudel.

**Recognitions**
Outstanding Teachers of the Year 2025 — more than 60 TSD educators were nominated; four winners were sent to Oakland Schools to represent Troy in the Countywide Outstanding Teacher Award program:

| Winner | Award | Building |
|---|---|---|
| Stephanie Everett | Preschool Teacher of the Year | TSD Preschool |
| Nancy Haboush | Elementary Teacher of the Year | Leonard Elementary School |
| Jamie Glab | Middle School Teacher of the Year | Smith Middle School |
| Staci Vought | High School & Overall Teacher of the Year | Athens High School |

A reception for nominees and winners was set for Wednesday, May 7th at Troy High School.

TSD Mission Moment — Troy High Model United Nations, a club of over 100 active members advised by Jacqueline Ciolek for the past ten years; officers recognized included Vinaya Gunasekar (President), Yeril Kim and Sanjay Shyamsundar (Vice Presidents), and Julia Triculescu (Secretary).

TSD Mission Moment — Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit, in its 68th year, established September 1956. Larson Middle School teacher David Egan spoke; thirteen students were introduced.

Robertson Homes donation — Dan Trudel, Assistant Superintendent of Business Services, introduced Tim Loughrin, Vice President of Land Acquisition, who presented a check for $7,750 to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence (TFEE), representing $250 for each of the 31 homes sold on property purchased from the Troy School District.

Student Spotlight — Athens senior Maaz Ali of the TSD Creative Guild; Creative Content Producer Thomas Butcher spoke.

Volunteer Appreciation — volunteers recognized from Athens High School (Michele Murto, Connie Ciak, Bidisha Goswami, Marc & Raquel Schriber), IA-East (Leslie McGill-Mayotte, Cristina German), and Troy High School (Chris & Denice Oliver, Kris Marshall, Kristine Rich).

**Autism Acceptance Month resolution**
Adopted 7 yes / 0 no, recognizing April 2025 as Autism Acceptance Month. Whereas clauses cite that Autism Spectrum Disorder affects more than five million people in the United States and that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report 1 in 36 children may have autism.

**Consent Agenda**
Moved by Mr. Haupt, supported by Mrs. Alic; items A through D approved 7-0: minutes of the March 4, 2025 Workshop; minutes of the March 8, 2025 Winter Retreat; minutes of the March 18, 2025 Board Meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for February 2025. Personnel and Curriculum: none.

**Business actions (all 7 yes / 0 no)**

| Item | Amount | Fund | Moved / Supported |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apple iPads and cases | $846,202.50 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund | Zendler / Potts |
| Temporary fencing — Fence Connection | $56,282.00 | 2023 Capital Projects Fund | Anne / Haupt |
| Smith Middle School furniture pilot | not to exceed $71,950 | 2023 Bond Fund | Potts / Anne |

The Smith furniture pilot was made through pre-existing bid contracts (consortiums).

**Other business**
One community member addressed the Board during non-agenda public communication; no action taken. Student representatives Adam McManus (Troy High), Diana D'Aloisio (Athens), and Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East) reported; Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School) was not in attendance. Board comments covered the open AARC survey, the May 6th workshop on writing curriculum, math program and AARC, federal funding cuts, Math 7 Parent Night, the TFEE Golf Outing on Tuesday, June 10th at Greystone Golf Course, and a call for help with 8th Grade Interviews. Dr. Philippart announced the next Board Workshop for Tuesday, May 6th at 6:00 p.m. at the Administration Building and the next Board of Education Meeting for Tuesday, May 20th at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building.

Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held April 22, 2025 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. In addition to Dr. Philippart, Board members Alic, Anne, Haupt, Melton, Potts, and Zendler were present. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Detmer, Keyser, Brennan, Pagel, and Trudel. Approximately 100 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 8:50 p.m. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Emina Alic, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carry the notation EA/jh.

RECOGNITION — OUTSTANDING TEACHERS. The Board congratulated the Outstanding Teachers of the Year for 2025. More than 60 TSD educators were nominated for the honor. Four nominees rose to the top for their commitment, passion, impact, and dedication, and these winners were sent to Oakland Schools to represent Troy in the Countywide Outstanding Teacher Award program. A short video of the district administrative team surprising the winners in their classrooms was shared with the community. The four honorees, each invited to the podium to speak and be photographed with Board members, were: Stephanie Everett, Preschool Teacher of the Year, TSD Preschool; Nancy Haboush, Elementary Teacher of the Year, Leonard Elementary School; Jamie Glab, Middle School Teacher of the Year, Smith Middle School; and Staci Vought, High School and Overall Teacher of the Year, Athens High School. Nominees and winners were invited to a reception on Wednesday, May 7th at Troy High School, where they would receive a certificate, their nomination packets, and a token of appreciation. TSD MISSION MOMENT — MODEL UNITED NATIONS. The Board recognized the Troy High Model United Nations team, an after-school club immersing students in international relations, diplomacy, politics, public speaking, and debate. The club has over 100 active members and is advised by Jacqueline Ciolek, who has led and grown the program for the past ten years. Students introduced were Vinaya Gunasekar (senior), President; Yeril Kim (senior), Vice President; Sanjay Shyamsundar (senior), Vice President; Julia Triculescu (junior), Secretary; Shreya Swaminathan (sophomore), Underclassmen Undersecretary; Isabella Doss (junior), Communications Director of PR and Social Media; Sarah Lee (junior), Video Communications Director; Shivani Angadi (senior), Middle School Outreach Director; Jeffrey Kim (senior), Aarush Kulkarni (junior), and Atul Ganesh (junior), Middle School Outreach Assistant Team; and Lauren Hatto (junior) and Pranavi Kumar (senior), Exceptional MUN Delegates and Leaders.

The Science and Engineering Fair of Metropolitan Detroit, now in its 68th year and established in September 1956, is one of the largest and oldest science fairs in the country. ROBERTSON HOMES DONATION. Dan Trudel, Assistant Superintendent of Business Services, noted that a Robertson Homes representative was present to present a check to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence. The donation was part of an agreement under which Robertson Homes would donate a portion of the sales proceeds from homes sold on property purchased from the Troy School District. Mr. Trudel introduced Tim Loughrin, Vice President of Land Acquisition, who presented a check in the amount of $7,750 to the TFEE, which was $250 for each of the 31 homes sold on that property. The Board accepted the check on behalf of the TFEE.

STUDENT SPOTLIGHT. The Board welcomed Athens senior Maaz Ali for his talents and contributions to the TSD Creative Guild Studio. Dr. Machesky invited Creative Content Producer Thomas Butcher to the podium.

VOLUNTEER APPRECIATION. In celebration of Volunteer Appreciation Month, the Board thanked dedicated volunteers whose students graduate from TSD this year. Those recognized with a certificate and token of appreciation were, from Athens High School, Michele Murto, Connie Ciak, Bidisha Goswami, and Marc and Raquel Schriber; from IA-East, Leslie McGill-Mayotte and Cristina German; and from Troy High School, Chris and Denice Oliver, Kris Marshall, and Kristine Rich.

AUTISM ACCEPTANCE MONTH. The Board adopted a resolution recognizing April 2025 as Autism Acceptance Month in the Troy School District, passing 7 yes and 0 no. The whereas clauses state that Autism Spectrum Disorder affects more than five million people in the United States; that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report 1 in 36 children may have autism; that autism is a neurological and developmental disorder characterized by social impairment and restricted interactive and communication behaviors that can affect anyone regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, or socioeconomic background; that symptoms may present in varied combinations with lifelong challenges in learning, daily living, employment, social-interactive behaviors, and understanding verbal and nonverbal communication; that physicians, psychologists, behavior analysts, speech and language pathologists, occupational therapists, vocational rehabilitation professionals, and educators can assist through early identification, education, intervention, and recreation; and that the district is committed to fostering acceptance and belonging.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS: none. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS): none.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.paragraph: A Troy School District curriculum recommendation dated May 2025, submitted by Natalie Haezebrouck and Lisa McDonald, presenting the K-5 elementary writing materials review and adoption proposal. Following a review that began in September 2024 and expanded a literacy leadership team to over 100 members in Spring 2025, the district recommends adopting The Writing Units of Study 2024, 2025, which 90% of the team chose as its top choice. The district's last writing adoption was in 2016; resources are to be available on the first day of school for the 2025-26 academic year.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
**Document**
Elementary Writing Materials Adoption, May 2025, submitted by Natalie Haezebrouck and Lisa McDonald for the Troy School District.

**Rationale**
Troy regularly reviews curricular materials and has updated its philosophy to look comprehensively at programming — instructional practices, intervention, assessment, and current data — rather than simply seeking new materials. CORE ELA programs have supported the five pillars of literacy (phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension) but historically offered limited support for writing instruction, so Troy has consistently implemented an additional writing curriculum alongside any reading program. The last writing adoption was in 2016.

**Comprehensive literacy system background**
Sections describe a strong elementary literacy leadership team; a professional learning community using common prep time, peer and vertical observations, district job-embedded lab days, and collaborative walk-throughs; high-quality classroom instruction with new-teacher onboarding in literacy, assessment and MTSS, district PD on handwriting, phonics and upper-grade word work/spelling, and Summer Homegrown Institutes; a system for assessing and monitoring progress (citing Afflerbach, 2007); effective and timely intervention within MTSS; family and community involvement; and access to high-quality preschool.

**Review process**
Fall 2024: a preschool-to-12th-grade literacy leadership meeting; expansion of job-embedded learning around writing instruction to an additional project school; ongoing PD in upper-grades word study/spelling, K-2 handwriting, norming and scoring of writing samples, and writing/phonics assessment. Spring 2025: the literacy leadership team expanded to over 100 members including representatives from all grade levels in each building, principals, literacy specialists, ELD specialists, special education, media specialists, and Teaching and Learning.

**Research and review tools**
Professional texts studied included "Creating a Classroom Vision for Teaching Writing" by Steve Graham (International Literacy Association), "Why Writing Workshops Work" by Zaner-Bloser, "Writing for Life: The Evidence Base for Powerful Writing Instruction" by Marisa Stukey, PhD and Elyse Eidman-Asdahl, PhD (National Writing Project), and "Teaching Elementary School Students to Be Effective Writers" from the What Works Clearinghouse (Institute of Education Sciences). Score cards and rubrics consulted were EdReports, the NYU Culturally Responsive Curriculum Score Card, The Reading League, and Knowledge Matters, alongside Michigan Writing and Language Standards. Data reviewed included demographic, process, perception (family and staff survey), and academic data (M-STEP target analysis and student writing samples), referencing "Beyond Testing" by Deborah Meier.

**Programs reviewed and team top-choice results**

| Program | Top choice |
|---|---|
| Writing by Design | 0% |
| Step-Up to Writing | 0% |
| Being a Writer | 4% |
| Benchmark Education Writing Workshop | 6% |
| Writing Units of Study | 90% |

Wit and Wisdom, Heggerty Bridge to Writing (K-3), and i-Ready Ready Writing (2-5) were excluded from review for lack of a cohesive K-5 program or limited rigor in writing instruction.

**Recommendation and early adoption**
The Writing Units of Study 2024, 2025 are recommended. Currently 24 teachers with representation in all 12 buildings and all grade levels are early adopting parts of the updated units, and all K-2 teachers have early adopted at least one updated writing unit. Among the early adoption team, 100% felt the updated Units of Study were helpful to them as teachers and responsive in their instruction, and 100% felt the units had a positive impact on student learning.

**Implementation plan**
All resources will be available for instruction on the first day of school for 2025-26. Training is offered in June and/or August through the Homegrown Institute, with an all-teacher kick-off during back-to-school PD in August 2025, followed by job-embedded professional learning and building-level literacy specialist support. Professional learning will focus on grammar and spelling components in grades 3-5, AI and digital writing in grades 3-5, unpacking new units, embedding phonics assessments and a spelling inventory in the K-5 assessment calendar, thin slicing of writing on-demands with adjusted rubrics, handwriting PD, balancing paper and digital writing, family engagement nights, and continued learning for support staff on writing intervention.
